observations.behavior: Replaces a per-file loop calling ducklake_add_data_files with a single recursive Parquet glob pattern passed to the same stored procedure.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces database round-trips and metadata flushes during warehouse ingestion; could improve throughput and reduce cancellation latency. This is an implementation change, not adoption or benefit proof.

observations.behavior: Updates tests to expect one registration call using a wildcard glob rather than multiple calls for individual files.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports regression checks for the new bulk-registration behavior. No independent evidence of runtime benefit without execution context.

observations.behavior: Adds assertions expecting exactly one registration SQL statement instead of N statements matching file count.
observations.posthog_connection: Checks that the workflow no longer emits separate commands per input file. Again, this does not establish actual performance gains or failure avoidance.

observations.limitations: Only documentation and test changes are shown alongside backend code. The production implementation relies on DuckLake's support for recursive globs and PostgreSQL compatibility; neither is demonstrated here. No metrics, benchmarks, or live-system observations accompany these hunks.

review.reason: The diff shows a substantive bounded improvement: replacing per-file registration with a single Parquet glob reduces database interactions and metadata commits. Tests were updated accordingly. However, tier 3 requires broader systemic risk reduction or cross-component demonstration absent from this chunk. Tier 1 would apply if only maintenance or docs changed; this has clear behavioral change. Confidence is moderate because we lack execution results or compatibility guarantees.
review.posthog_relevance: Changes warehouse ingestion efficiency and could reduce latency/cost during managed warehouse imports. This matters to PostHog users relying on timely warehouse refreshes but remains an engineering optimization rather than proven benefit.
review.uncertainty: Assessment depends on whether DuckLake supports the proposed glob syntax and how PostgreSQL handles bulk metadata insertion without row-count mismatches. These compatibility details are not supplied.
